## 347655: exact threshold, complete public-counterpart bridge

Primary: Kaul–Mudrock–Pelsmajer, arXiv:2008.08926v2, Conjecture 9; final Australasian J. Combin. 80(3) (2021) 419–441, Conjecture 1.9, printed p424. Equitable means each color used at most ceil(n/k), for every assignment of exactly k colors per vertex; color classes induce forests. It does NOT require a proper coloring or equally sized classes for an arbitrary color palette. The final introduction and extension lemma/proof were read, not merely the abstract. Theorem 1.6 only gives k>=p; Proposition 1.8 improves to p-1. Neither settles all p. My initial suspicion that the source already proves the exact threshold was overturned by the actual body.

Route A, single-vertex greedy: since at most floor(p/2) colors occur twice in the previous p vertices, k>=ceil((p+1)/2) gives a color with at most one previous neighbor of that color. This preserves a forest (a newly added vertex has at most one earlier monochromatic neighbor). It does not bound total color use by ceil(n/k). Saturated colors can consume the available choices. This proves only a nonequitable helper and is not a full solution.

Route B, remove k initial vertices and give them distinct colors: the established extension lemma needs |N(v_i) outside S|<=2i-1. For S the first k vertices this quantity can be p-k+i, which at i=1 is p-k+1, generally greater than1 at the conjectural k. Failure of this sufficient lemma is not a counterexample. Increasing to 2k vertices and retaining two uses of each color avoids this bottleneck.

Actual public proof: https://probxiv.com/problems/on-equitable-list-arboricity-of-graphs-3, full HTML and text saved. Thus every v has the literal record property. In the source predicate, an independent J in C5 has size0,1 or2. So C5 has no source-isolatable vertex. This example lies outside the target's C4 hypothesis and is NOT a refutation of335666. It proves a real definition discrepancy, not automatic target falsity or a credited correction.

First route, transplant girth>=5 obstruction: if source-isolatable x is isolated by J, delete the independent copy J in one prism layer. The remaining copy x in that layer is a leaf supported by the other x. To contradict well-coveredness via lemma2.1 one tries to make another leaf at that support. Source theorem3.8 obtains the needed sets from disjoint second neighborhoods A_i around N(x). In girth4 those A_i can overlap; triangle-freeness alone does NOT make them disjoint. Also lemma3.2 requires the second factor to have order at least3, so cannot be applied with K2. These are exact unpaid hypotheses, not just a failed heuristic.

Second route, an exact combinatorial reformulation: any independent set of G square K2 is uniquely A in layer1 and B in layer2, where A,B are independent in G and A intersect B is empty (the vertical edges). It is maximal iff every vertex outside A union B has a neighbor in A AND a neighbor in B. Proof: an unchosen vertex in layer1 is vertically dominated when it belongs to B, and otherwise needs a neighbor in A; layer2 is symmetric. Conversely these domination conditions cover every unchosen vertex. Hence the prism is well-covered iff all disjoint independent pairs satisfying V minus(A union B) subset N(A) intersect N(B) have the same total cardinality |A|+|B|. This is an exact equivalence for arbitrary finite graphs, not merely a one-way helper.

For any maximal independent A of G, choose a maximal independent B of G-A. Then A,B are disjoint and every vertex outside their union is dominated by A (A maximal in G) and B (B maximal in G-A). Thus they form a prism-maximal pair. Well-coveredness of the prism forces |A|+|B|=t for every such pair. For a source-isolation witness J with remainder{x}, A=J union{x} is maximal independent in G, giving one family of pairs; a full contradiction would need another pair of different total size.
